evidence.timingScope: Five alternating pairs of 1,200 alignment calls per case and border style, with Lua garbage collection paused inside each timed phase. Borrowed native methods, live anchor geometry and pure phase output are modeled. Full renderer, group and combat regressions run separately. Reported time is neither an in-game callback measurement nor FPS.

parity: R186 reuses the nearby-panel records that match either prepared layout. In both styles, 60 repeated scans of a stable seven-panel HUD and 60 alternating warmed strip widths cut 420 new panel records to zero. Sixty new widths create 300 records and retain the same 60 alignment graphs. The native-style rectangle reads, changed decorative boxes and final coordinates match. The phase fixture models panel geometry and does not measure the whole border rebuild.
rules: Match the existing frame, border owner, role, layer priority, scale and four public stroke coordinates before reusing an input record. Read live geometry on every alignment pass. The planner keeps its temporary nodes outside the retained records, and the output phase keeps the existing native writes and failure recovery. Removing the last owner shortens the active list and restores its border.
nativeAcceptance: Live held-action crossings, rapid drops, group join and leave, seams and combat taint remain pending. Unchanged-panel scans in the desktop model establish the cost of that phase during unrelated HUD or unit reflows.
